properties.headline: Coastal Flood Statement issued October 5 at 4:00AM EDT until October 5 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor saltwater flooding.

* WHERE...Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets
and lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.
properties.instruction: Do not drive through flooded roadways.

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 2:56AM CDT until October 5 at 6:00AM CDT by NWS Mobile AL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southern Okaloosa County in northwestern Florida...
Southern Santa Rosa County in northwestern Florida...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM CDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 255 AM CDT, Doppler radar and automated rain gauges indicated
heavy rain due to thunderstorms. Minor flooding is already
occurring in the advisory area. Between 2 and 3 inches of rain
have fallen.
- Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wright, Fort Walton Beach, Niceville, Destin, Eglin AFB, Pace,
Valparaiso, Gulf Breeze, Mary Esther, Bagdad, Ocean City, Lake
Lorraine, Oriole Beach, Navarre, Shalimar, Cinco Bayou, Navarre
Beach, Pea Ridge, Floridatown and Wynnehaven Beach.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:

* WHERE...Northeast Florida Beaches.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through late Wednesday night.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away

properties.instruction:

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Shoal River Near Crestview affecting Okaloosa County.

For the Shoal River...including Crestview...Minor flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Shoal River near Crestview.

* WHEN...From Monday evening to Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 8.5 feet, Water in yards on Sowel Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 8:15 PM CDT Sunday the stage was 5.6 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tomorrow evening to a crest of 8.4 feet Tuesday morning. It will
then fall below flood stage Thursday morning.
- Flood stage is 8.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 8.4
feet on 04/26/2020.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:

The next statement will be issued when updates occur.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 4 at 8:48PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
...The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Florida...Georgia...

St Mary's River At Macclenny affecting Nassau, Charlton and Baker
Counties.

Additional information is available at
https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX

The next statement will be issued Monday evening at 900 PM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Mary's River at Macclenny.

* WHEN...From Monday morning until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Minor flooding of low lying areas and
timber lands including some properties along St. Mary's River Bluff
Road and the Cypress Landing Resort on the Georgia side. At 14.0
feet, Flooding of bottomlands along the river and some lower access
roads including the lower half of St. Mary's River Bluff Road which
cuts off 15 to 20 homes on the Georgia side. At 15.0 feet, Flooding
begins to impact the lower end of Steel Bridge Road on the Florida
side and cuts off access to the river gage as well as access to
several homes. At 16.0 feet, Access roads on both sides of the
river in Florida and Georgia are flooded, including the entire low
lying stretch of St. Mary's River Bluff Road on the Georgia side
which cuts off 40 to 50 homes. On the Florida side, the lower end
of St. Mary's Cove Road past the public boat ramp becomes flooded
and cuts off access to 20 to 30 homes. The Stokes Road Bridge over
the river is generally closed due to high water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 PM EDT Sunday the stage was 10.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage late
tomorrow morning and continue rising to a crest of 14.0 feet
Tuesday evening.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast Alabama, including the following
areas, Geneva and Houston, Florida, including the following areas,
Calhoun, Central Walton, Coastal Bay, Coastal Franklin, Coastal
Gulf, Coastal Jefferson, Coastal Wakulla, Gadsden, Holmes, Inland
Bay, Inland Franklin, Inland Gulf, Inland Jefferson, Inland
Wakulla, Jackson, Leon, Madison, North Walton, Northern Liberty,
South Walton, Southern Liberty and Washington, and Georgia,
including the following areas, Baker, Ben Hill, Berrien, Brooks,
Calhoun, Colquitt, Cook, Decatur, Dougherty, Early, Grady, Irwin,
Lanier, Lee, Lowndes, Miller, Mitchell, Randolph, Seminole,
Terrell, Thomas, Tift, Turner and Worth.

* WHEN...Through Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Additional rainfall totals of 2 to 4 inches are forecast for most
of the area with locally higher amounts of up to 6 inches
possible through Monday, especially along the Emerald and
Forgotten Coasts. Another area of concern is across south-central
Georgia where locally heavy rainfall since Friday afternoon has
primed the region more so than the rest of our area, so it wont
take as much rain to cause flash flooding. Across the flood watch
area, very high rain rates due to the tropical air mass may lead
to flash flooding, especially in urban and poor drainage areas.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
